content: Site Enhancement Oil (SEO) is a liquid substance, typically composed of a mixture of oils, that is utilized by some bodybuilders to artificially increase the visible size of certain muscles. The effects of SEO are entirely cosmetic in nature, with no functional or performance-related benefits. The oil is administered via injection, either subcutaneously (under the skin) or intramuscularly (between the muscle fibers). The mechanism of action involves the oil filling the muscle tissue, creating the appearance of increased muscle volume. This process is referred to as site injection, meaning the oil is injected directly into the specific muscle that the individual wishes to enlarge. SEO is often used to enhance a muscle that appears underdeveloped compared to the rest of the body. However, the effects are temporary. Once the use of SEO is discontinued, the perceived gains in muscle size are lost as the oil is gradually absorbed by the muscle tissue. It is important to note that SEO is not an androgenic substance and does not contain anabolic steroids. Instead, it is simply an oil-based compound. Despite its cosmetic purpose, the oil can remain in the body for years, potentially causing long-term damage to the muscle tissue. This damage often results in scarring of the muscle, which can lead to permanent structural changes. In essence, SEO is a purely aesthetic intervention that creates scar tissue within the muscle, giving the illusion of a well-trained and developed physique, without any actual improvement in muscle strength or function.
